The test image shows a dark green sugarcane leaf with prominent pale/cream-white longitudinal streaks running parallel to the veins, plus small scattered reddish spots. This pattern suggests a streak/mosaic viral disease.

Top candidates: Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv, Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus, Leaf_Scald, Yellow_Leaf. Now I'll view one reference per class.

Analysis of the 4 references vs test image:

- **Test image**: Dark green sugarcane leaf with bright white/cream longitudinal streaks running parallel to veins + small reddish-orange spots
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv** ref: Subtle mottled/mosaic pattern, diffuse light-dark intermingling — less distinct than test
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus** ref: Yellow-green diffuse mottling — doesn't match the sharp white streaks
- **Leaf_Scald** ref: Distinct bright white/pale stripe running along the leaf — closely matches the test image's white longitudinal streaks on dark green
- **Yellow_Leaf** ref: Overall leaf browning/yellowing — clearly different

The test image's bright white longitudinal stripes on a dark green leaf with small reddish spots is the classic presentation of Leaf Scald (Xanthomonas albilineans), which causes characteristic white pencil-line stripes along the veins. This matches the Leaf_Scald reference much better than the diffuse mosaic patterns of the other candidates.
